subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining work fix the scheduler/memory producer that emits invalid maintenance read paths, or broaden read-tool behavior for directory and missing-reference maintenance reads after live proof confirms the leak?
rationale: Current source proves only partial daily-memory mitigation, while OpenClaw policy treats fallback/read semantics and runtime hot-path behavior as compatibility-sensitive product choices when the producer boundary is unclear.

options.title: Live repro, then fix the producer
options.body: Collect a current-main cron or heartbeat reproduction with tool-call paths and memory growth, then repair the path generator or maintenance prompt that emits stale, wrong-root, or directory-as-file reads.

options.title: Define a read-tool maintenance fallback
options.body: If maintainers want these maintenance reads to be tolerated, explicitly define the narrow path contract and add tests so ordinary invalid reads still fail.

options.title: Fold into broader Gateway memory-leak work
options.body: If live proof shows RSS growth is not caused by these read errors, keep this as evidence under the broader Gateway memory leak investigation instead of making a path-specific fix.

recommendation.title: Live repro, then fix the producer
recommendation.body: Collect a current-main cron or heartbeat reproduction with tool-call paths and memory growth, then repair the path generator or maintenance prompt that emits stale, wrong-root, or directory-as-file reads.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses current Gateway/runtime policy and memory-flush ownership, and this person appears in recent current-main and memory plugin history for those paths.
